entries.word: Don't count your chickens before they are hatched.
entries.def: Don't anticipate the future too much.

entries.word: Don't put all your eggs in one basket.
entries.def: Don't invest all your efforts, or attention in just one thing.

entries.word: Never judge a book by its cover.
entries.def: Don't judge people/things by their outward appearance.

entries.word: Never look a gift-horse in the mouth.
entries.def: Never refuse good fortune when it is there in front of you.

entries.word: Take care of the pence and the pounds will take care of themselves.
entries.def: Take care of small sums of money and they will become large sums.

entries.word: When the cat's away, the mice will play.
entries.def: [people will take advantage of someone else's absence to behave more freely]

entries.word: You can lead a horse to water but you can't make it drink.
entries.def: [you can try to persuade someone, but you can't force them]

entries.word: One swallow doesn't make a summer.
entries.def: [one positive sign does not mean that all will be well. A swallow is a very fast-flying bird that returns to Britain in late spring]

entries.word: There's no smoke without fire. or Where there's smoke, there's fire.
entries.def: [rumours are usually based on some degree of truth]

entries.word: Too many cooks spoil the broth
entries.def: [too many people interfering is a bad way of doing things]

entries.word: People who live in glass houses shouldn't throw stones.
entries.def: [don't criticise others' faults if you suffer from them yourself]
[a lot of people helping makes a job easier]
